title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
authors: Guo C, Pleiss G, Sun Y, Weinberger KQ
finding: Modern neural networks can be miscalibrated; temperature scaling is a strong simple post-hoc baseline.
limit: In-distribution benchmark setting; calibration under shift requires separate evidence.

title: Can You Trust Your Model's Uncertainty? Evaluating Predictive Uncertainty Under Dataset Shift
finding: Accuracy and calibration degrade under dataset shift; ordinary post-hoc calibration can fall short, while model-marginalizing approaches are comparatively strong.
limit: Natural-image/general ML benchmark, not surgical.

title: Simple and Scalable Predictive Uncertainty Estimation using Deep Ensembles
authors: Lakshminarayanan B, Pritzel A, Blundell C
finding: Independent ensembles provide a simple high-quality predictive-uncertainty baseline without full Bayesian inference.
limit: Compute/storage cost scales with number of models.

title: Dropout as a Bayesian Approximation: Representing Model Uncertainty in Deep Learning
finding: Inference-time dropout can approximate Bayesian model uncertainty using repeated stochastic forward passes.
limit: Approximation quality and calibration are task/model dependent.

title: What Uncertainties Do We Need in Bayesian Deep Learning for Computer Vision?
finding: Provides the widely used aleatoric/epistemic distinction and models both in computer vision.
limit: The conceptual decomposition is useful, but practical disentanglement is model-dependent.

title: Uncertainty Estimation in Medical Image Classification: Systematic Review
finding: MC dropout and deep ensembles were the most frequently used UQ methods; metrics and evaluation practice were heterogeneous.
limit: Classification-only review covering literature through 2021.

title: A review of uncertainty quantification in medical image analysis: Probabilistic and non-probabilistic methods
authors: Huang L, Ruan S, Xing Y, Feng M
finding: Medical-imaging UQ spans probabilistic, ensemble, deterministic, calibration and other strategies with task-dependent evaluation.
limit: Broad review; not surgical-specific.

title: Uncertainty quantification for artificial intelligence in medical imaging: what every radiologist needs to know
finding: Distinguishes prediction confidence from UQ and highlights triage, thresholding, calibration, computational cost and prospective-validation challenges.
limit: Radiology-focused and narrative, not surgical.

title: Confidence Calibration and Predictive Uncertainty Estimation for Deep Medical Image Segmentation
method: Calibration and predictive uncertainty for FCNs
finding: Medical segmentation networks can be poorly calibrated and overconfident on correct and erroneous pixels; calibration/UQ must be evaluated explicitly.
limit: Non-surgical datasets.

title: Improving Calibration and Out-of-Distribution Detection in Deep Models for Medical Image Segmentation
method: Multi-task calibration + spectral feature OOD detection
finding: Multi-task training improves calibration and spectral feature-map signatures can identify OOD segmentation inputs.
limit: Medical imaging rather than surgical video.

title: Failure Detection in Deep Neural Networks for Medical Imaging
finding: Frames failure detection as identifying likely model errors rather than merely identifying OOD inputs.
limit: Not surgical and method/task-specific.

title: Uncertainty Estimation for Safety-critical Scene Segmentation via Fine-grained Reward Maximization
finding: Direct surgical evidence that scene-segmentation uncertainty/calibration can be optimized while preserving task accuracy using one-pass inference.
limit: Method-specific; does not by itself establish robustness under the full P0.4 shift suite.

title: Surgical Phase Recognition in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy
method: Calibrated confidence for dynamic model switching
finding: Calibrated confidence is already used operationally in surgical phase recognition to choose between models.
limit: Does not systematically evaluate reliability across natural/controlled distribution shifts.

title: When Surgery Meets the Unknown: Uncertainty-Aware Open-Set Recognition for Surgery Phase Classification
authors: Geyer S, Kalogeiton V, Roitberg A
method: Benchmark of open-set algorithms + evidential GEAR
finding: Open-set surgical phase recognition and uncertainty-aware rejection are already directly studied on cholecystectomy data.
limit: Open-set unknown-class setting differs from covariate-shift failure prediction.

title: Scene graph-guided uncertainty decomposition improves confidence calibration in surgical visual question answering
finding: Direct surgical evidence combines uncertainty decomposition, calibration and selective answering; reported accuracy 63.58%, ECE 16.97%, risk-coverage AUC 0.0861.
limit: VQA differs from phase recognition/segmentation and uses constructed scene-graph pipeline.

title: Meta-SurDiff: Classification Diffusion Model Optimized by Meta Learning is Reliable for Online Surgical Phase Recognition
finding: Emerging work explicitly models frame-level uncertainty for online phase recognition across five datasets.
limit: Preprint; reliability/calibration claims require peer-reviewed confirmation.

title: OpenMIBOOD: Open Medical Imaging Benchmarks for Out-Of-Distribution Detection
authors: Gutbrod M, Rauber D, Nunes DW, Palm C
type: Medical OOD benchmark with surgical domain
method: 24 post-hoc OOD methods across 3 medical benchmarks
finding: PhaKIR is a dedicated endoscopy benchmark with smoke covariate shift plus near/far OOD datasets; rankings from natural-image OOD do not directly transfer to medical imaging.
limit: OOD detection is not the same as predicting whether a surgical model output is wrong.

title: A Baseline for Detecting Misclassified and Out-of-Distribution Examples in Neural Networks
finding: Provides the canonical simple confidence baseline for error/OOD detection.
limit: OOD membership and prediction error are related but not equivalent.

title: Energy-based Out-of-distribution Detection
finding: Energy scores provide a strong post-hoc/energy-based baseline for OOD detection.
limit: General benchmark; medical/surgical performance must be verified rather than assumed.

title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
method: Confidence-based reject option with risk control
finding: Formalizes the accuracy/risk versus coverage trade-off for deep classifiers with rejection.
limit: General classification; task-specific confidence for segmentation/temporal outputs differs.

title: SelectiveNet: A Deep Neural Network with an Integrated Reject Option
method: Integrated selection head and coverage objective
finding: End-to-end selective prediction can optimize risk–coverage rather than using only post-hoc thresholds.
limit: Requires retraining; deployment constraints may favor post-hoc monitors.

title: Selective Prediction for Semantic Segmentation under Distribution Shift
authors: Borges BLC, Pacheco BM, Silva D
finding: Selective prediction for semantic segmentation under distribution shift is already directly evaluated in medical imaging.
limit: Workshop paper; not surgical-specific.

title: Soft Dice Confidence: A Near-Optimal Confidence Estimator for Selective Prediction in Semantic Segmentation
authors: Borges BLC, Pacheco BM, Silva D
finding: Provides a theoretically motivated image-level confidence estimator for Dice-oriented selective segmentation and evaluates six medical-imaging tasks including OOD scenarios.
limit: Image-level abstention may be too coarse for surgical overlays; not surgical-specific.

title: Learning to Abstain: Reliable Medical Image Segmentation With Rejection Option
authors: Sanisoglu MA, Navab N, Kim ST
finding: Directly trains segmentation models to abstain on uncertain pixels and reports improved accepted-pixel Dice across coverage levels.
limit: Non-surgical medical segmentation; pixel-level abstention has different human-interface implications.

title: Conformal selective prediction with cost aware deferral for safe clinical triage under distribution shift
method: Temperature scaling + split/Mondrian/weighted CP + cost-aware deferral
finding: A combined calibrated conformal deferral pipeline reduces retained-case error at 80% coverage by 49.6% ID and 46.7% OOD; weighted CP is most robust under temporal shift.
limit: Tabular sepsis triage, not imaging/surgery; weighted CP assumes access to unlabeled target covariates.

title: Uncertainty Sets for Image Classifiers Using Conformal Prediction
authors: Angelopoulos AN, Bates S, Jordan M, Malik J
finding: Conformal prediction can wrap a classifier to achieve finite-sample marginal coverage under exchangeability with efficient label sets.
limit: Coverage guarantee relies on calibration/test exchangeability unless using shift-aware variants.

title: Conformal Prediction Under Covariate Shift
authors: Tibshirani RJ, Barber RF, Candès EJ, Ramdas A
finding: Coverage can be extended to covariate shift using likelihood-ratio weighting when the shift assumptions and density ratios are available/estimable.
limit: Assumes covariate-shift structure and reliable weighting; not arbitrary concept shift.

title: Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift
finding: Adaptive conformal inference targets long-run coverage under time-varying distributions without ordinary exchangeability.
limit: Long-run frequency control differs from per-case or subgroup guarantees.

title: Distribution-free, Risk-controlling Prediction Sets
authors: Bates S, Angelopoulos A, Lei L, Malik J, Jordan MI
finding: Extends finite-sample risk control beyond simple classification coverage to general losses including image segmentation.
limit: Holdout calibration and risk definition are central; not a surgical deployment guarantee by itself.

title: Conformal Prediction for Image Segmentation Using Morphological Prediction Sets
finding: Model-agnostic conformal mask margins provide coverage-controlled segmentation uncertainty on medical applications.
limit: Binary masks; morphology-based coverage does not directly solve instance-level surgical segmentation.

title: Conformal forecasting for surgical instrument trajectory
finding: Direct surgical guidance work applies CP/CQR to instrument trajectory forecasts with coverage/interval-size evaluation and multiple-testing corrections.
limit: Trajectory forecasting, not phase recognition or image segmentation; in-house data.

title: A critical perspective on finite sample conformal prediction theory in medical applications
finding: Marginal finite-sample coverage can be practically misleading with small one-time calibration sets because calibration-set-conditional coverage varies substantially.
limit: Does not invalidate conformal theory; clarifies what the standard marginal guarantee does and does not mean.

title: Reliable Uncertainty Under Class Imbalance and Distribution Shift: Class-Conditional Conformal Prediction of Multiple Sclerosis
method: Marginal vs class-conditional CP across scanner/degradation shifts
finding: Marginal CP can hide severe minority-class undercoverage: at 1.5T, MS coverage was 16.9% vs 95.2% controls; class-conditional CP improved MS coverage to 77.5%.
limit: Preprint and non-surgical; even class-conditional coverage remained below nominal under severe shift.

title: Beyond Uncertainty: Generalizable Failure Monitoring for Surgical Segmentation under Acquisition Degradation
authors: Pham HD, Cao DPM, Huynh TT
topic: Failure monitoring + conformal calibration under shift
method: TCSR-Monitor: confidence + shape + temporal consistency + image quality; Mondrian conformal calibration
finding: Directly targets confident surgical segmentation failures under acquisition degradation; within corrupted frames reports AUROC 0.946 versus entropy 0.594 and shows severity-aware conformal calibration, but false alarms remain substantial.
limit: Very recent; EndoVis 2017/corruption benchmark; global threshold false alarms up to ~40% at moderate corruption and SAM2 transfer limitations.

title: Measuring Calibration in Deep Learning
finding: Calibration conclusions can depend strongly on binning, class conditioning, probability selection and norm; ECE alone is insufficient.
limit: General classification.

title: A Novel Characterization of the Population Area Under the Risk Coverage Curve (AURC) and Rates of Finite Sample Estimators
finding: Formalizes AURC as a principal metric for evaluating selective classifiers across coverage thresholds.
limit: General classification; segmentation risk must be defined task-appropriately.
